title: Rondeau
identity: Mouret’s Rondeau is the opening movement of his 1729 Symphonies and Fanfares for the King’s Supper. The catalog names a Lloyd Conley saxophone arrangement; the opened Musicnotes preview is a distinct Bill Galliford version in E-flat for alto saxophone and piano, from Easy Classical Themes Level 1.

evidence.claim: The Musicnotes listing identifies a four-page alto saxophone/piano digital arrangement by Bill Galliford, in E-flat major, from Easy Classical Themes Level 1; this is one arrangement and is not confirmed as the catalog’s edition.

Opened the Musicnotes product page and visually inspected its first public score-preview page. The preview is Bill Galliford’s four-page E-flat alto saxophone and piano arrangement from Easy Classical Themes Level 1, not confirmed as the catalog’s Lloyd Conley arrangement.

score_observations: In the first page of the Bill Galliford preview, the saxophone rests through the piano introduction and enters near the end of the displayed opening page. The visible page is in 4/4, marked Maestoso at quarter note = 152, and the saxophone entrance shows a short slurred figure followed by a sustained note. This observation applies to the Galliford version only; the catalog’s Lloyd Conley edition was not inspected.
review_focus: The opening piano introduction delays the saxophone entrance; inspect the catalog’s Lloyd Conley version for its actual form and part before comparing it with this modern arrangement.
collection_flag: Transcription of a Baroque orchestral movement. One listed adaptation is explicitly part of a beginner-themed series; this does not establish the intended edition or all arrangements.

score_links.description: Public Musicnotes viewer; first score-preview page visually inspected. This is the Galliford arrangement, not matched to the catalog’s Lloyd Conley entry.

gaps: College/professional or pedagogical placement was not verified.
The catalog’s Lloyd Conley edition was not located or visually inspected; no performance recording was verified.
